words.gloss: is indeed of the nature of

literal: Having embraced I lay; I moved aside; at that very moment, to scoop and take, indeed like, spread the pallor.
translation: I lay in his embrace, but the moment I turned aside, the pallor of separation spread over me so thickly that it could be scooped up by the handful.
modern: நான் என் காதலரைத் தழுவிக்கொண்டு படுத்திருந்தேன்; அவரிடமிருந்து சற்றே விலகினேன்; அந்த நொடியிலேயே, அள்ளி எடுக்கும் அளவுக்குப் பசலை நிறம் என் மேல் படர்ந்துவிட்டது.
explanation: This couplet vividly describes the heroine's intense sensitivity to even the briefest separation from her lover. She explains that she was lying in a close embrace, but the very instant she turned or moved slightly aside, the pallor of separation (pacappu) rushed to cover her body. The poet uses a striking hyperbole, stating that the sallow spots spread so thickly in that split second that they could be scooped up by the handful (aḷḷikkoḷ). This highlights how her physical and emotional well-being is entirely dependent on constant union with her beloved.
